---
title: "Statistics"
---

Notes on probability, inference, and statistical modelling.

Work through the foundations first, then move into modelling and uncertainty.

## Learning order

1. [Probability, Distributions, and Sampling](probability-distributions-sampling.qmd) — populations, samples, random variables, and dependence.
2. [Mean and Variance](mean-and-variance.qmd) — centre and spread.
3. [Estimation and Confidence Intervals](estimation-confidence-intervals.qmd) — estimates, standard errors, and interval interpretation.
4. [Hypothesis Testing](hypothesis-testing.qmd) — null models, errors, power, and p-values.
5. [Regression, Linear Models, and GLMs](regression-linear-glm.qmd) — prediction, effects, outcome distributions, and diagnostics.
6. [Causal Inference](causal-inference.qmd) — assumptions needed for causal claims.
7. [Marginal and Conditional Effects](marginal-and-conditional-effects.qmd) — interpreting effects across subgroups and covariate values.
8. [Mixed Models and Resampling](mixed-models-resampling.qmd) — clustered data, bootstrap, and permutation methods.

## Further resources

- [OpenStax Introductory Statistics](https://openstax.org/details/books/introductory-statistics-2e) — accessible core reference.
- [NIST Engineering Statistics Handbook](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/) — detailed methods and diagnostics.
